# The Best Friends and Fables Alternatives in 2026: An Honest Roundup

If you've been playing on Friends and Fables and started searching for an alternative, you're in good company. Friends and Fables, built by the indie studio Side Quest Labs, has carved out a real audience as an AI tabletop RPG platform with an AI Game Master named Franz, deep worldbuilding tools, and multiplayer up to six players. But a lot of players hit the same set of walls: combat is off by default while the team rebuilds it, the retrieval based memory system can lose track of details over a long campaign, and premium narration and image models run on a credit economy that adds up. So they go looking.

results.title: 6 Best Multiplayer AI Games in 2026 (Play With Friends) | Altworld
results.content:
### Can you play AI games with friends?

Yes, though most AI games are single-player. Altworld runs shared persistent worlds joined by invite link, Friends & Fables runs D&D-style campaigns with an AI DM for groups, and FableAI and Hidden Door support co-op story sessions.

### Is there a free multiplayer AI game?

Altworld sessions are free to start — the host shares an invite link and friends join in the browser. Friends & Fables and Hidden Door also offer free tiers for group play.

### What is a multiplayer AI game?

A game where multiple human players share one AI-driven experience — the AI narrates, simulates, or referees a world that all players act in, either in real time or turn by turn.

Keep reading [...] ## 3. Hidden Door — social story worlds

Hidden Door's curated story worlds are built social-first: friends co-star in narrative adventures inside classic and licensed settings, with the AI keeping arcs coherent. Less sandbox, more shared-improv-with-a-good-director.

 Multiplayer shape: co-op narrative sessions
 Best for: story nights inside worlds you already love
 Price: free to try

## 4. FableAI — co-op adventures with narration and art

FableAI's co-op mode lets friends run illustrated, voice-narrated adventures together — the most presentation-forward group option, and phone-friendly, which matters when half the party is on mobile.

 Multiplayer shape: co-op story adventures
 Best for: casual group sessions with production value
 Price: free tier; subscription [...] ## 1. Altworld — shared persistent worlds by invite link

Altworld multiplayer is the full simulation, shared: the host opens a world, sends a link, and friends create characters inside the same persistent timeline — same factions, same economy, same rumor mill. Because state is structured rather than chat-based, the world stays canonical no matter who acts: if your friend burns a warehouse, its absence is a fact of \your\ run too. Sessions continue across days, and the same engine drives solo play, so a shared world feels identical to the game you already know.

 Multiplayer shape: shared persistent world, turn-based, invite link — no accounts needed to try
 Best for: living in one timeline together over days or weeks
 Price: free to start; Candles fuel turns
